name: audio
description: SFX and music playback: one-shot sounds, loops, and interruptible sources via one AudioSystem
postInstallNotes:
## audio installed

**Runtime wiring.** Create one `ContentAudioPlayer` per screen and register the single `AudioSystem` in your update pipeline (position does not matter — it only talks to the audio backend):
```csharp
var audioPlayer = new ContentAudioPlayer(content);
pipeline.Add(new AudioSystem(world, audioPlayer));
```
Dispose the player with the screen (after the pipeline) to release live instances.

**One-shot SFX** (button click, hit feedback) — publish a message, no entity needed:
```csharp
world.Publish(new PlaySoundRequest("Sounds/click", volume: 0.8f));
```

**Lifecycle playback** (looping ambience, interruptible music) — put an `AudioSourceComponent` on an entity:
```csharp
entity.Set(new AudioSourceComponent("Sounds/wind", loop: true));
// cut it: entity.Get<AudioSourceComponent>().State = AudioPlaybackState.Stopped;
// or remove the component / dispose the entity — playback stops immediately.
```

**Content.** Add `.wav` (or `.ogg`) files to your `.mgcb` with the built-in importer — no extra `/reference:` lines needed:
```
#begin Sounds/click.wav
/importer:WavImporter
/processor:SoundEffectProcessor
/build:Sounds/click.wav
```

**No audio hardware?** `ContentAudioPlayer` degrades to a silent no-op (single warning log) so headless/CI runs keep working.

**Premises:** `docs/premises.md`
